question.text: Dihydrogen of high purity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mo>></mo><mn>99</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>95</mn><mo> </mo><mo>%</mo></mrow></mfenced></math> is obtained through :

options.text: The electrolysis of acidified water using <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Pt</mi></math> electrodes.

solution.text: Dihydrogen of high degree of purity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mo>></mo><mn>99</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mfenced><mi></mi></math> is obtained by the electrolysis of warm aqueous barium hydroxide solution between nickel electrodes.
